title: 1982 AHSME Problem 24
statement: In the adjoining figure, the circle meets the sides of an equilateral triangle at six points. If \(AG=2,\) \(GF=13,\) \(FC=1\) and \(HJ=7,\) then \(DE\) equals

solutions.text:
First, power of \(A\) gives \(AH(AH+7)=AG\cdot AF.\) The latter product is \(2\cdot15=30,\) so \(AH=3,\) \(BJ=6,\) and \(BH=13.\) Let \(BD=u,\) \(DE=x,\) \(EC=v.\) From the secants at \(B\) and \(C,\) \[ \begin{aligned} u(u+x)&=BH\cdot BJ\\ &=13\cdot6=78,\\ v(v+x)&=CF\cdot CG\\ &=1\cdot14=14. \end{aligned} \] Also \(u+x+v=16.\) Subtracting the power equations and using the sum gives \(u-v=4.\) Hence \(u=10-\frac{x}{2}\) and \(v=6-\frac{x}{2}.\) Substitution into \(v(v+x)=14\) gives \(x^2=88,\) so \(DE=2\sqrt{22}.\)

Therefore, the correct answer is A.
hints: All three sides of the triangle have length \(16\)
Apply power of a point from \(A,\) \(B,\) and \(C\) to relate the two base segments and \(DE\)
